correctness.rationale: Conditional on k observed negative leaves, the OR of the remaining m=n-k has positive probability u_m=1-(1-p)^m and posterior p/u_m per remaining source when positive. A positive-side decision flip improves correctness by [2p-u_m]_+, so the stated general root gain follows by multiplying by the probability (1-p)^k and by m/n. For k=0, u_n/p decreases strictly from n to 2-2^(1-n) as p rises to one half, giving the unique crossing of 2 for n>=3. With q=1-p and n=3, three times the marginal accuracies are D=(3p[-1+3p-p^2]_+,2p^2q,pq^2,0). Leaf pairs without the root have concave coverage and affine accuracy. With the root, coverage is constant; the two accuracy curvatures are (D2-2D1+D0)/3 and (D3-2D2+D1)/3. The first numerator is pq(1-5p) below the posterior crossing at (3-sqrt(5))/2 and p(p+2)(2p-1) above it; the second is 2pq(2p-1). Thus exactly p<1/5 is irreparable. For p>=1/5, the remaining pair conditions give the maximum of zero and (D_(k+1)-D_k)/(3pq^k) for k=0,1,2; the last bound is -1/3. Comparing the other two bounds gives all four stated pieces and the matching endpoint values; the cutoff is always less than one. Two leaves yield D=(2p^2,pq,0), strictly negative root-present leaf curvature, and only the possible positive bound (1-3p)/2. One leaf yields duplicate readings and no obstruction.
